Rumours suggest Apple will launch a brand-new MacBook Ultra this autumn as part of its ever-expanding "Ultra" product line. Here are six new features expected from the MacBook Ultra.

#1: All-new design, thinner and lighter than MacBook Pro

Bloomberg points out that Apple's new MacBook model is a "complete redesign," thinner and lighter than the current MacBook Pro.

The MacBook Ultra was originally expected to launch under the "MacBook Pro" brand but with an all-new design. Although that possibility still remains, current rumours are pointing towards the "Ultra" branding.

We don't know whether the ports will be reduced compared to the MacBook Pro, but it's quite likely. That said, I'd be surprised if Apple pushed the "thin and light" design to extremes, since the MacBook Ultra is likely to attract plenty of professional users.

#2: M5 Pro and M5 Max chips

There had been widespread expectation that the all-new M6 chip series would debut on the MacBook Ultra. But recent rumours tell a different story.

Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reports that Apple has abandoned plans for the M6 Pro and M6 Max chips, and has instead accelerated development of high-end M7 chips.

So although future MacBook Ultra models will feature M7 chips, this year's model is reportedly sticking with the existing M5 Pro and M5 Max chips from the MacBook Pro.

#3: Touchscreen — a first in Mac history

Touch support is finally coming to the Mac. And the MacBook Ultra will be the first model to feature a touchscreen.

According to Mark Gurman, Apple is adding touch functionality to the Mac as a supplementary input method, not as a replacement for the keyboard and trackpad.

macOS Golden Gate comes with numerous optimisations, offering a more touch-friendly interface that works equally well for users without a touchscreen.

#4: OLED display

Every iPhone now comes with an OLED display, and the iPad Pro also gained a stunning tandem OLED in 2024. Yet the Mac has been the exception — until now.

The MacBook Ultra will adopt OLED, becoming the first Mac to feature this display technology.

OLED should deliver deeper blacks, better contrast, and improved off-angle viewing, and may also help the MacBook Ultra extend its battery life.

#5: Dynamic Island

The 2021 MacBook Pro was the first Mac to feature a "notch," but the MacBook Ultra is expected to drop this design.

The new MacBook Ultra is expected to ditch the "notch" in favour of a hole-punch camera cutout, along with a new software feature: Dynamic Island.

Like on the iPhone, Dynamic Island both masks the camera cutout through software and offers new functionality for macOS — including serving as the home for Siri AI.

Wildcard #6: Cellular option with C2 modem

Apple has yet to release a Mac with cellular connectivity. But rumours suggest this may be about to change.

In a late-2024 report on Apple's in-house cellular modem plans, Mark Gurman wrote:

Of course, there's no guarantee the Mac will gain cellular capability this year, but with Apple's C2 modem set to appear in the iPhone 18 Pro this autumn, the timing seems to line up perfectly.

Which new feature of the MacBook Ultra are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
